passage: Chen ate lunch on the steps behind the gym because the cafeteria felt like a stage. Three boys had started calling him "ghost", and by now he believed nobody at school wanted him around. In the library, Oskar from the chess club slid a spare board across the table. "Black or white?" Chen shrugged, then played. On the walk home he heard himself say, quietly, "They are being mean to me." Oskar only nodded and said his sister had been teased once too. The next week Chen told the chess teacher what was happening, and the steps behind the gym were no longer the only place he could eat.

qa.a: He ate lunch on the steps behind the gym.

qa.q: How did Chen feel after the boys started calling him "ghost"?
qa.a: Chen felt lonely and unwanted; he believed nobody at school wanted him around and ate lunch on the steps behind the gym instead of the cafeteria.

qa.q: What helped Chen feel less alone, and what did he do next?
qa.a: A boy from the chess club offered him a game, and Chen said out loud that they were being mean to him and then told the chess teacher.

qa.q: What might Oskar be thinking when he nods and mentions his sister was teased?
qa.a: Oskar may want Chen to know he is not the only one it has happened to and that Oskar understands, which makes him a safe friend.

grounding: A bullied child feels nobody wants him, then finds one safe friend and a club and says it aloud.
